blurb: Lithium-ion and beyond — energy, power, cycle life, safety, and cost trade-offs across rechargeable, primary, and grid-scale chemistries.
question: Which battery chemistry fits this product?
title: Battery Chemistries: A Practical Reference
lede: A battery is a chemistry packaged as an electrochemical system — electrodes, electrolyte, and cell engineering traded off against energy, power, life, safety, and cost. This guide catalogs {{N_ENTRIES}} chemistries across seven classes, from mass-produced lithium-ion to flow batteries and research frontiers.

facets.label: Application
facets.tip: Directional tags for where each chemistry is mainly used or targeted today — not exhaustive.

facets.label: Energy
facets.tip: Typical cell-level gravimetric energy density band (system-level for flow batteries). Format, generation, and chemistry tuning shift real products within and across bands.

facets.label: Cycle life
facets.tip: Directional full-cycle life to ~80% capacity at moderate rate, depth of discharge, and temperature — real conditions can shift this by multiples. Primary (non-rechargeable) chemistries carry no tag.

facets.label: Cost
facets.tip: Directional average price per kWh: cell-level for mainstream rechargeables, system-level for flow and grid products, contained energy at street prices for primaries, and sample-scale pricing for pilot/R&D chemistries. Real quotes move with volume, format, and commodity prices.

facets.label: Maturity
facets.tip: Mass production = multi-GWh global supply chains · Commercial = established products at smaller scale · Pilot = demonstration or early commercial · R&D = lab and startup stage.
